learning_path:
**6-Month Data Science Learning Path**

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1-2 weeks | COU5245 | Data Science Fundamentals with Python and SQL Specialization | Coursera | Foundational building blocks: Python, SQL, and data science basics |
| 2-4 weeks | COU4368 | Introduction to Data Science Specialization | Coursera | Gradual increase in complexity: data science concepts and Python programming |
| 4-6 weeks | COU1615 | Expressway to Data Science: Python Programming Specialization | Coursera | Practical application and project-based learning: Python programming and data science |
| 6-8 weeks | COU4033 | Applied Data Science Specialization | Coursera | Emphasis on data storytelling and communication: data analysis and visualization |
| 8-12 weeks | COU4120 | Python Packages for Data Science | Coursera | Gradual increase in complexity: intermediate-level data science concepts and Python packages |
| 12-16 weeks | COU3806 | Python Data Products for Predictive Analytics Specialization | Coursera | Practical application and project-based learning: predictive analytics and data visualization |
| 16-20 weeks | COU4602 | Data Visualization with Python | Coursera | Emphasis on data storytelling and communication: advanced data visualization techniques |
| 20-24 weeks | COU4997 | Basic Data Processing and Visualization | Coursera | Gradual increase in complexity: intermediate-level data processing and visualization |
| 24-26 weeks | COU1665 | Google Advanced Data Analytics Capstone | Coursera | Practical application and project-based learning: advanced data analytics and machine learning |
| 26 weeks | COU1600 | The Nuts and Bolts of Machine Learning | Coursera | Advanced concepts: machine learning and deep learning |

This 6-month learning path starts with foundational courses in data science, Python, and SQL (COU5245 and COU4368). The next phase focuses on practical application and project-based learning with courses on Python programming (COU1615) and data science (COU4033). The path then increases in complexity with intermediate-level courses on data science concepts (COU4120 and COU3806) and data visualization (COU4602 and COU4997). The final phase emphasizes advanced concepts in machine learning (COU1665) and deep learning (COU1600). This learning path covers the full duration requested, with at least one course per period, and follows the core educational principles of gradual increase in complexity, practical application, and emphasis on data storytelling and communication.
expanded_query: "Data Science Fundamentals" is a 6-month course designed for learners with a strong foundation in programming (prerequisite: Python programming skills) and basic statistics. This course covers essential skills and topics in data science, including data wrangling, visualization, and machine learning using popular libraries such as Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, and Scikit-learn. Students will learn to work with large datasets, develop predictive models, and communicate insights effectively through data storytelling. By the end of the course, learners will be able to design and implement data-driven solutions, analyze complex data sets, and make informed business decisions.

learning_path:
**Learning Path for Cloud Computing Infrastructure and DevOps Deployment**

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | EDX2556 | Google Cloud Computing Foundations: Cloud Computing Fundamentals | edx | Foundational knowledge of cloud computing |
| 2 | EDX1394 | Google Cloud Computing Foundations: Infrastructure in Google Cloud | edx | Understanding of Google Cloud infrastructure |
| 3 | EDX2010 | DevOps and Software Engineering Capstone Project | edx | Hands-on experience with DevOps and software engineering |
| 4 | EDX2306 | Reliable Google Cloud Infrastructure: Design and Process | edx | Designing and deploying reliable cloud infrastructure |
| 5 | EDX1059 | Getting Started with Terraform for Google Cloud | edx | Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and automation |
| 6 | EDX3178 | IBM Cloud Essentials | edx | Understanding IBM Cloud infrastructure and services |
| 7 | EDX2309 | Back-end Application Development with Node.js and Express | edx | Building server-side applications with Node.js and Express |
| 8 | EDX946 | Guided Project: Get Started with Containers and Registries | edx | Hands-on experience with containers and registries |
| 9 | EDX741 | AWS: Getting Started with Cloud Security | edx | Understanding cloud security on AWS |
| 10 | EDX2661 | Introduction to DevSecOps for Managers | edx | Understanding DevSecOps and its importance for managers |
| 11 | EDX1536 | Introduction to Cloud Foundry | edx | Understanding Cloud Foundry and its capabilities |
| 12 | EDX959 | Cloud Cost Management: Optimization Strategies | edx | Optimizing cloud costs and resource utilization |

The learning path starts with foundational knowledge of cloud computing (EDX2556) and progresses to understanding Google Cloud infrastructure (EDX1394). Hands-on experience with DevOps and software engineering is gained through EDX2010, followed by designing and deploying reliable cloud infrastructure (EDX2306). Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and automation are introduced through EDX1059, and understanding IBM Cloud infrastructure and services is covered in EDX3178. Building server-side applications with Node.js and Express is learned in EDX2309, and hands-on experience with containers and registries is gained through EDX946. Understanding cloud security on AWS is covered in EDX741, and the importance of DevSecOps for managers is introduced in EDX2661. Finally, understanding Cloud Foundry and its capabilities is learned in EDX1536, and optimizing cloud costs and resource utilization is covered in EDX959.

This learning path provides a comprehensive understanding of cloud computing infrastructure and DevOps deployment, covering foundational knowledge, hands-on experience, and advanced topics. The courses are chosen to build upon each other, with each course providing a solid foundation for the next one.

The target duration of this course is approximately 12 weeks, with a mix of lectures, hands-on labs, and project-based learning.

**How the path fits together**

This learning path is designed to take the learner from foundational data engineering concepts to advanced applications in data engineering. The first period focuses on building a solid understanding of data engineering basics, including the responsibilities and skillsets of a data engineer. The second period applies these concepts through a capstone project, focusing on data warehousing and ETL processes. The third period introduces Apache Spark and its role in data engineering and machine learning. The fourth period covers big data concepts, Hadoop architecture, and Spark programming basics. The fifth period delves into advanced SQL topics, while the sixth period explores advanced Spark programming and its applications in big data computing. The seventh period introduces programming paradigms and their applications in data engineering. The eighth period covers lean enterprise framework and its applications in data engineering. The ninth period explores emerging technologies and their applications in data engineering. Finally, the tenth period applies data engineering skills in business systems analysis. This path provides a comprehensive understanding of data engineering concepts and their applications in various domains.

The target duration of this course is approximately 12 weeks, with a focus on hands-on projects and real-world applications.

**Learning Path**

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | EDX509 | Circuits for Beginners | edx | Foundational knowledge of circuits and electronics |
| 2 | EDX478 | Circuits and Electronics 1: Basic Circuit Analysis | edx | Builds on EDX509, introducing node method, superposition, and Thevenin method |
| 3 | EDX206 | AC and Switching Circuits | edx | Expands on EDX478, covering AC circuits and switching circuits |
| 4 | EDX861 | Circuits and Electronics 2: Amplification, Speed, and Delay | edx | Introduces amplifiers, speed, and delay in circuits, building on EDX206 |
| 5 | EDX2320 | Fundamentals of Transistors | edx | Covers transistor fundamentals, essential for understanding modern electronics |
| 6 | EDX1475 | Primer on RF Design | edx | Introduces RF design principles, building on EDX2320 |
| 7 | EDX361 | Electromagnetic Compatibility Essentials | edx | Covers electromagnetic compatibility, essential for designing and testing electronic systems |
| 8 | EDX2180 | Linear Algebra II: Matrices and Linear Transformations | edx | Provides linear algebra skills, essential for understanding and working with electronic systems |
| 9 | EDX2093 | MATLAB Essentials | edx | Introduces MATLAB, a popular tool for electronic system design and analysis |
| 10 | EDX3038 | Designing Electronics for Recycling in a Circular Economy | edx | Covers design principles for electronic systems in a circular economy |

The learning path starts with foundational knowledge of circuits and electronics in EDX509, followed by EDX478, which introduces more advanced circuit analysis techniques. EDX206 expands on this knowledge, covering AC circuits and switching circuits. EDX861 introduces amplifiers, speed, and delay in circuits, building on EDX206. EDX2320 covers transistor fundamentals, essential for understanding modern electronics. EDX1475 introduces RF design principles, building on EDX2320. EDX361 covers electromagnetic compatibility, essential for designing and testing electronic systems. EDX2180 provides linear algebra skills, essential for understanding and working with electronic systems. EDX2093 introduces MATLAB, a popular tool for electronic system design and analysis. Finally, EDX3038 covers design principles for electronic systems in a circular economy, applying the knowledge gained throughout the path.
expanded_query: In this course, students will gain a comprehensive understanding of electrical engineering fundamentals, covering the essential topics of circuits, signals, and electronics. Prerequisites include a strong foundation in algebra and trigonometry, as well as basic programming skills. Through a combination of theoretical and practical instruction, students will develop skills in circuit analysis, signal processing, and electronic device design, including topics such as Ohm's Law, Kirchhoff's Laws, and the behavior of AC and DC circuits. This course is designed to be completed in approximately 12 weeks, providing students with a solid foundation for further study in electrical engineering and related fields.

expanded_query: "Chinese for Business Travelers: Beginner Level" is a 6-week course designed for individuals with no prior knowledge of the Chinese language. This course covers essential skills and topics, including basic Chinese characters, pronunciation, and grammar, as well as business-related vocabulary and phrases, such as introductions, directions, and basic transactions. Students will learn to communicate effectively in everyday business situations, including ordering food, making reservations, and navigating cultural differences. By the end of the course, students will be able to hold basic conversations and read simple Chinese texts, preparing them for successful business travel in China.

### 6-Month Data Science Learning Path

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1-2 weeks | COU3198 | Python for Data Science, AI & Development | Coursera | Foundational building block: Python programming |
| 2-4 weeks | COU1615 | Expressway to Data Science: Python Programming Specialization | Coursera | Build on Python programming with data science concepts |
| 4-6 weeks | COU4368 | Introduction to Data Science Specialization | Coursera | Introduce data science concepts, including data visualization and SQL |
| 6-8 weeks | COU4072 | Fractal Data Science Professional Certificate | Coursera | Focus on data storytelling and communication |
| 8-10 weeks | COU4983 | Data Science: Statistics and Machine Learning Specialization | Coursera | Introduce machine learning and statistical concepts |
| 10-12 weeks | COU4602 | Data Visualization with Python | Coursera | Focus on data visualization and presentation |
| 12-14 weeks | COU4997 | Basic Data Processing and Visualization | Coursera | Practice data processing and visualization |
| 14-16 weeks | COU673 | Data Wrangling with Python Project | Coursera | Apply data wrangling and visualization skills to a project |
| 16-18 weeks | COU5705 | Advanced Data Analysis and Collaboration in Qlik Sense | Coursera | Advanced data analysis and collaboration skills |
| 18-20 weeks | COU5943 | Advanced Data Analysis and Visualization with Pandas | Coursera | Advanced data analysis and visualization with pandas |
| 20-24 weeks | COU4983 | Data Science: Statistics and Machine Learning Specialization | Coursera | Review and practice machine learning and statistical concepts |

This 6-month learning path starts with foundational courses in Python programming (COU3198) and data science concepts (COU1615 and COU4368). The path then focuses on data storytelling and communication (COU4072), machine learning and statistical concepts (COU4983), data visualization and presentation (COU4602), data processing and visualization (COU4997), data wrangling and visualization (COU673), advanced data analysis and collaboration (COU5705), and finally advanced data analysis and visualization with pandas (COU5943). The path is designed to gradually increase in complexity, with regular milestones and assessments to track progress and maintain motivation.
expanded_query: "Data Science Fundamentals" is a 6-month course designed for learners with a strong foundation in programming (prerequisite: Python programming skills) and basic statistics. This course covers essential skills and topics in data science, including data wrangling, visualization, and machine learning using popular libraries such as Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, and scikit-learn. Students will learn to extract insights from complex data sets, develop predictive models, and communicate findings effectively through data storytelling. By the end of the course, learners will be able to apply data science techniques to real-world problems and make informed decisions using data-driven insights.

learning_path:
**6-Month Data Science Learning Path**
=====================================

### Period 1: Foundational Building Blocks (Weeks 1-4)

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | COU5245 | Data Science Fundamentals with Python and SQL Specialization | Coursera | Introduces the basics of data science, including probability and statistics, data visualization, and regression analysis. |
| 1 | COU1615 | Expressway to Data Science: Python Programming Specialization | Coursera | Focuses on Python programming, a fundamental skill for data science. |

### Period 2: Data Structures and Statistics (Weeks 5-8)

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | COU4377 | What is Data Science? | Coursera | Expands on the data science concepts introduced in Period 1, covering big data, machine learning, and deep learning. |
| 2 | COU3198 | Python for Data Science, AI & Development | Coursera | Builds on the Python programming skills developed in Period 1, introducing data analysis and AI concepts. |

### Period 3: Data Wrangling and Visualization (Weeks 9-12)

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3 | COU4948 | Data Wrangling with Python Specialization | Coursera | Focuses on data wrangling, a critical skill for data science, using Python. |
| 3 | COU1070 | Data Literacy: Exploring and Visualizing Data Specialization | Coursera | Introduces data visualization and storytelling, essential for communicating insights to non-technical stakeholders. |

### Period 4: Machine Learning and Advanced Topics (Weeks 13-18)

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4 | COU1427 | Applied Data Science with Python Specialization | Coursera | Covers intermediate-level machine learning concepts, including text mining and predictive modeling. |
| 4 | COU4602 | Data Visualization with Python | Coursera | Expands on data visualization skills, introducing more advanced techniques and tools. |

### Period 5: Specialized Topics and Project-Based Learning (Weeks 19-24)

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5 | COU4983 | Data Science: Statistics and Machine Learning Specialization | Coursera | Covers advanced statistics and machine learning concepts, including regression analysis and ensemble learning. |
| 5 | COU6169 | Python Project for Data Science | Coursera | Focuses on practical project-based learning, applying data science concepts to real-world problems. |

### Period 6: Capstone and Final Project (Weeks 25-26)

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 6 | COU1665 | Google Advanced Data Analytics Capstone | Coursera | Provides a comprehensive capstone experience, integrating all previously learned concepts and skills. |

This 6-month learning path follows the recommended educational principles:

* Foundational building blocks: Periods 1-2 focus on the basics of data science, programming, and statistics.
* Gradual increase in complexity: Periods 3-5 introduce more advanced concepts, such as machine learning, data visualization, and data wrangling.
* Practical application and project-based learning: Periods 4-6 emphasize hands-on projects and real-world applications.
* Emphasis on data storytelling and communication: Periods 3-5 focus on data visualization and storytelling.
* Regular assessment and feedback: Learners will receive regular assessments and feedback throughout the learning path.
* Pacing and time management: The learning path is broken into manageable chunks, with a balance of theoretical and practical components, to ensure learners can maintain a consistent pace and stay motivated throughout the 6-month period.
expanded_query: "Data Science Fundamentals" is a 6-month course designed for learners with a strong foundation in programming (prerequisite: Python programming skills) and basic statistics. This course covers essential skills and topics in data science, including data wrangling, visualization, and machine learning using popular libraries such as Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, and scikit-learn. Students will learn to extract insights from complex data sets, develop predictive models, and communicate findings effectively through data storytelling. By the end of the course, learners will be able to apply data science techniques to real-world problems and make informed decisions using data-driven insights.

expanded_query: In this course, students will develop a comprehensive understanding of nutrition and healthy eating principles grounded in scientific evidence. Prerequisites include a basic understanding of human biology and prior knowledge of nutrition is not required. Through lectures, discussions, and case studies, students will learn to critically evaluate the scientific literature on nutrition, identify evidence-based recommendations for healthy eating, and develop skills in nutrition assessment, planning, and counseling. Topics will include macronutrient and micronutrient requirements, dietary patterns and their impact on chronic disease, and the role of nutrition in maintaining optimal health across the lifespan. The target duration of this course is 12 weeks.

learning_path:
**Learning Path for Public Health and Epidemiology Basics**

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | COU3773 | Epidemiology: The Basic Science of Public Health | Coursera | Foundational understanding of epidemiology and its role in public health. |
| 2 | COU3404 | Data and Health Indicators in Public Health Practice | Coursera | Understanding data collection methods and health indicators is essential for epidemiology. |
| 3 | COU2329 | Outbreaks and Epidemics | Coursera | Building on the previous courses, this one introduces outbreak investigation and statistics. |
| 4 | COU1586 | Measuring Disease in Epidemiology | Coursera | Understanding disease measurement is crucial for epidemiological analysis. |
| 5 | COU315 | Biostatistics in Public Health Specialization | Coursera | Biostatistics is a fundamental skill for public health professionals, and this course provides a solid introduction. |
| 6 | COU1172 | Surveillance Systems: Analysis, Dissemination, and Special Systems | Coursera | Surveillance systems are critical for public health, and this course covers data collection and analysis. |
| 7 | COU5018 | Investigating Epidemics like COVID-19: An Analyst's Guide | Coursera | This intermediate-level course applies epidemiological concepts to real-world scenarios, including COVID-19. |
| 8 | COU5934 | Study Designs in Epidemiology | Coursera | Understanding study designs is essential for evaluating epidemiological research and making informed decisions. |

**How the path fits together:**

This learning path starts with foundational courses in epidemiology and public health, gradually building skills in data collection, analysis, and interpretation. The path then introduces biostatistics and surveillance systems, essential tools for public health professionals. Finally, the intermediate-level course on investigating epidemics and the advanced course on study designs provide learners with the skills to apply epidemiological concepts to real-world scenarios and evaluate research. This path provides a comprehensive introduction to public health and epidemiology basics for non-clinicians.

learning_path:
**Learning Path for Climate Science and Energy Transition**

| Period | Course ID | Course Title | Platform | Why this course |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | COU3101 | Climate Science for Everyone | Coursera | Foundational understanding of climate science |
| 2 | COU1459 | Energy, Environment, and Everyday Life | Coursera | Introduction to energy and environment concepts |
| 3 | COU2507 | Introduction to Environmental Science Specialization | Coursera | Interdisciplinary connections between climate science and environmental science |
| 4 | COU6590 | Global Energy and Climate Policy | Coursera | Understanding global energy and climate policy |
| 5 | COU419 | Bending the Curve: Climate Change Solutions 2 | Coursera | Practical applications of climate change solutions |
| 6 | COU4475 | Ecological and Energy Transitions in Southern Countries | Coursera | Advanced understanding of ecological and energy transitions in specific contexts |
| 7 | COU4610 | Predicting Extreme Climate Behavior with Machine Learning | Coursera | Skill-building progression in data analysis and machine learning |
| 8 | COU5734 | Corporate Sustainability. Understanding and Seizing the Strategic Opportunity | Coursera | Understanding corporate sustainability and strategic opportunities |
| 9 | COU6381 | Python Functions, Files, and Dictionaries | Coursera | Skill-building progression in programming and data evaluation |
| 10 | COU5736 | Climate Solutions: UAE | Coursera | Real-world applications of climate solutions in specific contexts |

The learning path starts with foundational courses in climate science and energy, such as COU3101 and COU1459. These courses establish a solid base of prior knowledge and introduce key concepts in climate science and energy.
